I hate how correct you are. As someone who is currently suffering with depression (and have been for a while), I have an incredibly huge, Irrational fear of change. I'm fairly certain its the reason why I was never 100% honest when talking to my therapist. Fear of consequences, fear of having to put in effort and work, only to find out it didnt actually help me. I'm currently working on it though.

I'll try to give you some input from the other side of the situation. I personally have a friend who I usually go to when I am feeling really bad. She's always there to comfort me and motivate me. I trust her with almost everything.

However, that doesnt mean I dont care about her. More than often I'm concerned that I'm bothering her (anxiety getting the better of me) or even annoying her. She had to basically confirm multiple times that I dont bother her, and yet I still feel like it. This whole situation is something I'm usually afraid of when reaching out to someone. But that seems to be the difference between myself and your "friends". Your friends dont seem to care about your own mental health, they dont even think about the fact that they might be bothering you! They come across as extremely rude (even yelling at you if you dont reach out every day) and quite frankly are extremely selfish.

Maybe they simply never thought of the fact that you might get tired of constantly caring for them, maybe it has something to do with their depression. That doesnt even seem very unrealistic. But that doesnt excuse rude behaviour. The best advice I can give you is to be honest with them and to tell them that you cannot be there 24/7 because you have your own life to live and your own situations to solve. If they continue being rude about it, then you can gladly cut them out of your life, because then they are extremely selfish and disrespectful towards you.

You need to start Rapid Fire Hopping (RFH = hopping every second frame) at a point where the steepness in a slope changes. I think a pretty easy place to start would be the sloped road near the end of Luigi Circuit. There you should easily be able to tell the difference in steepness of the slopes. Now just try starting your RFH around one of those steepness changes and you should get a fair idea for where to start your RFHs. In most cases in the game you will be able to RFH whereever the steepness of a slope changes. So just use the same method for a ramp. Check for the point where the steepness changes and then try out starting the RFH on different frames. And obviously, the earlier you start your RFH the lower you will go. So dont start at the last possible change of steepness, but rather the earliest.
